The first automobile depends on the definition used. If considering early steam-powered road vehicles, the first was built in 1769 by French inventor Nicolas-Joseph Cugnot [d6, d7, d8]. However, the first practical, marketable automobile using an internal combustion engine is credited to Karl Benz of Germany, who received a patent on January 29, 1886 [d1, d2, d6]. In the United States, the first successful gasoline automobile was designed in 1893 by Charles and Frank Duryea [d3, d4].
